knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 5.1.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Outline: given a conjugate prior and likelihood, how do you obtain the posterior (family + updated parameters at a high level)?
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Multiply prior × likelihood (or use conjugate update formulae); renormalise; read updated parameters of the same family.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 5.1.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Binomial n=10 with x=3 successes and Beta(2,2) prior. (1) State the posterior distribution (parameters). (2) Refuse: 'Bayesian means I believe in Bayes' without a posterior, and 'having the posterior distribution finishes choosing the Bayesian point estimator under squared-error loss.'
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) Posterior Beta(2+3, 2+7) = Beta(5,9). (2) Refuse slogan-Bayes — produce an actual posterior distribution (or its parameters). The posterior is the full distribution; a loss-based point estimator (e.g. posterior mean under squared-error loss) is a further step.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Slogan-Bayes without a posterior, or jumping to a point estimator as if it were the posterior.
